title: Finality-sentinel and continuity-token protocol for streaming output continuity
creator: Maya Patel
description: Multiple recent customer escalations across Hosted and Dedicated exposed cases where streamed SSE responses terminated before application-level completion. Symptoms: final token(s) missing, clients receive truncated JSON outputs, or the connection closes without an explicit final event. Root causes observed in production include: (1) edge/LB drain and HTTP/2 multiplexing interaction that drops final flush frames, (2) runtime backpressure that triggers mid-request resource reclamation, and (3) subtle differences in newline/framing semantics between our runtime and some client SDKs. This ticket defines a protocol (finality-sentinels and continuity-tokens), server-side guards, SDK heuristics, and an operational rollout to make streaming output durable and resumable across transient disconnects.
proposed_fix: Introduce a lightweight finality-sentinel event appended after model final token emission (sentinel = '<<FINALITY-SENTINEL:v1>>') to mark definitive end-of-output at the runtime layer.
Attach monotonic continuity-token headers to streaming sessions (X-Continuity-Token) which encode last-acked token-offset + short stable checksum to permit idempotent resume attempts.

On graceful disconnect, runtime should persist a 30s soft-fence checkpoint (in-memory hotspot + optional redis backing for hosted) keyed by continuity-token; clients may reconnect with the token to request missing suffixes.
Edge proxy and LB config: ensure HTTP/1.1 chunked and HTTP/2 DATA frames are not coalesced away on connection drain; add a 250ms drain-hold for finality-sentinel propagation.

Client SDK changes: implement resume-on-reconnect heuristic that, upon seeing network close without sentinel, reopens stream with continuity-token and merges in idempotent tail only when checksums match.
Fallbacks: if token mismatch or checkpoint unavailable, expose retry-with-abandon header so calling app can request deterministic rerun or accept degraded output.
Instrumentation: add events for sentinel-emitted, sentinel-missing, continuity-token-created, resume-attempts, and resume-success-rate.
Automated e2e tests that inject LB drain jitter, simulated backpressure reclamation, and SDK reconnection to assert no out-of-order or duplicated tokens in reconstructed output.
acceptance_criteria: Hosted nightly canaries exercising LB drain jitter show 0 observed truncated-final-output incidents for target workloads (chat and streaming generation templates) over 72h
Client SDKs (js/python/ruby) successfully resume >95% of transient disconnects in CI harness when sentinel absent but checkpoint available
Telemetry dashboard surfaces sentinel-missing rate and continuity-token resume-success, with alert when sentinel-missing > 0.1% of streams
Runbook updated with playbook for customer escalations referencing continuity-token and how to extract checkpoints.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): implement server-side sentinel + token and deploy to 10% of hosted runtime fleet behind a feature flag; instrument metrics. (1 week)
Phase 2 (SDK): release client SDKs with resume heuristics and optional opt-in flag; request a small set of early adopter customers to enable. (1 week)
Phase 3 (LB tuning): coordinate infra to apply 250ms drain-hold globally for streaming endpoints; monitor for latency regressions. (3 days)
Phase 4 (Gradual ramp): increase server rollout to 50% then 100% after 72h of stable telemetry and reduced customer escalations. (2 weeks total)
Phase 5 (Dedicated/Private): provide configuration guide and small patch to Dedicated runtime; for Private deploys include migration script and compatibility shim. (parallel)
qa_tests: Simulate sudden TCP reset mid-stream and assert SDK resume reconstructs identical token sequence when checkpoint exists
Inject LB drain during final 200ms of response and assert finality-sentinel is received by client or recoverable via continuity-token
Run chaos tests with concurrent streams at 10k RPS to validate checkpoint memory footprint and eviction behavior
Compatibility test against older SDKs to ensure graceful degradation (clients that don't understand sentinel still see usable outputs)
telemetry: Emit 'sentinel_emitted' event with runtime_id, request_id, model, seq_offset
Continuity token gauge and resume_attempts counter with labels outcome=success|failure
Dashboard: streaming-integrity with panels for sentinel_missing_rate, resume_success_rate, post-resume-duplication-rate
